column1: How is the triangle inequality for the vector infinity norm proven for a sum $x+y$?

column1: How is the distance between two $n$-dimensional vectors $x$ and $y$ defined using norms?

column1: Definition: Convergence of a vector sequence $P_k$ to a limit $P$.
column2: The sequence converges if $\lim_{k \to \infty} \|P_k - P\| = 0$ for a chosen vector norm.

column1: In $R^n$, how does the choice of vector norm affect the limit of a convergent sequence?
column2: It does not; the limit is independent of the selection of the vector norm.

column1: A vector sequence $P_k$ converges to $P$ if and only if each \_\_\_\_\_ of $P_k$ converges to the corresponding component of $P$.
Why is the norm of the difference $\|P_k - P\|$ useful in numerical analysis?
column2: It provides a way to check if a generated sequence is 'close enough' to the limit to stop the computation.
